_**User (2026-10-21 23:31:55Z)**_

Let stores configure how long failed workflow executions are kept #67

User Story
As a developer running a Medusa store, I want to set how long failed workflow executions are kept, or turn it off, so that I can balance debugging history against database size.

User Scenario
A developer runs a high-traffic store and only needs one day of failure history. They set the failure retention option on the workflow engine module in medusa-config to one day and restart. Failed executions now disappear after a day instead of seven. Another developer who doesn't want any extra rows sets it to 0, and failed runs are deleted when they finish, like before.

Acceptance Criteria
Both workflow engine modules (in-memory and Redis) accept a failure retention option, in seconds, in their module options in medusa-config.
When the option is set to a positive number, kept FAILED and REVERTED executions are saved with that retention window instead of the default.
When the option is set to 0, FAILED and REVERTED executions are deleted when they finish, the same as before Add retention for failed and reverted workflow executions #16.
When the option isn't set, the default window from Keep failed and reverted workflow executions by default #66 is used.
A workflow that sets its own retentionTime still uses its own value, whatever the option is set to.
Automated tests in both engines verify a custom window, a value of 0, and the default when the option isn't set.
Out of Scope
A setting for this in the admin dashboard.
Different windows per workflow. Workflows can already do that with retentionTime.
Changing how often the cleanup runs.
Open Questions
What should the option be called? Something like failedExecutionRetention reads clearly next to the existing retentionTime.
Should a negative or non-number value fail at startup with an error, or fall back to the default?

This is an issue I am going to start working on. Can you review the spec to make sure it is clear enough to implement and that it fits into the code? It is a follow up to this issue, which has not been implemented yet:

<pasted_content id="54db">
Keep failed and reverted workflow executions by default #66

User Story
As a store manager, I want failed and reverted workflow executions to still be there after they finish, so that I can open one and see which step failed and what rolled back without reading server logs.

User Scenario
A customer reports that their checkout failed. The store manager opens Settings > Workflows in the admin. Today the list is empty, because the failed run was deleted the moment it finished. With this change, the failed execution is in the list. The manager opens it, and the existing timeline shows the step that failed in red and the steps that were compensated after it.

Acceptance Criteria
When a workflow that doesn't set its own retentionTime finishes as FAILED or REVERTED, its execution is saved instead of deleted, and it is returned by GET /admin/workflows-executions.
A kept failed or reverted execution is saved with a default retention window of 7 days, so the existing clearExpiredExecutions cleanup removes it after that window.
A workflow that finishes as DONE without its own retentionTime is still deleted when it finishes, the same as today.
A workflow that sets its own retentionTime keeps using that value for every end state, the same as today.
Criteria 1 to 4 hold in both the in-memory engine (workflow-engine-inmemory) and the Redis engine (workflow-engine-redis), with tests for each engine.
Opening a kept failed execution in the admin shows the failed step and the compensated steps in the existing timeline, with no dashboard changes.
Automated tests in both engines verify that failed and reverted executions are kept with the default window, done executions are still deleted, and a workflow's own retentionTime still wins.
Out of Scope
Letting stores change or turn off the 7 day window. That's Let stores configure how long failed workflow executions are kept #67.
Cancelling or retrying executions (Add workflow lifecycle controls to the admin API and dashboard #23).
Any dashboard changes. The list and timeline already exist.
A new cleanup job. clearExpiredExecutions already runs every 30 minutes in both engines and deletes finished executions once their retention_time passes.
Open Questions
Is 7 days the right default, or should it be shorter to keep the table small on busy stores?
Child workflow executions (ones with parentStepIdempotencyKey) are already saved today. Should they get the same default window?
</pasted_content id="54db">

import { ContainerLike } from "@medusajs/framework"
import { Logger } from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import { FlowCancelOptions } from "@medusajs/framework/workflows-sdk"

export type InitializeModuleInjectableDependencies = {
  logger?: Logger
}

export type WorkflowOrchestratorCancelOptions = Omit<
  FlowCancelOptions,
  "transaction" | "transactionId" | "container"
> & {
  transactionId: string
  container?: ContainerLike
}
import { Logger } from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import { QueueOptions, WorkerOptions } from "bullmq"
import { RedisOptions } from "ioredis"

export type InitializeModuleInjectableDependencies = {
  logger?: Logger
}

/**
 * Module config type for the Redis Workflow Engine.
 *
 * The workflow engine uses three queues internally:
 * - **Main queue**: Handles workflow retries, step timeouts, and transaction timeouts
 * - **Job queue**: Handles scheduled workflow job execution
 * - **Cleaner queue**: Handles periodic cleanup of expired workflow executions
 *
 * You can configure shared options that apply to all queues/workers, or provide
 * per-queue overrides for fine-grained control.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // Simple configuration - same options for all queues
 * {
 *   redisUrl: "redis://localhost:6379",
 *   queueOptions: { defaultJobOptions: { removeOnComplete: 1000 } },
 *   workerOptions: { concurrency: 10 }
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // Advanced configuration - per-queue overrides
 * {
 *   redisUrl: "redis://localhost:6379",
 *   // Shared defaults
 *   workerOptions: { concurrency: 10 },
 *   // Override for job queue (scheduled workflows)
 *   jobWorkerOptions: { concurrency: 5 },
 *   // Override for cleaner (low priority)
 *   cleanerWorkerOptions: { concurrency: 1 }
 * }
 * ```
 */
export type RedisWorkflowsOptions = {
  /**
   * Redis connection string
   * @deprecated Use `redisUrl` instead for consistency with other modules
   */
  url?: string

  /**
   * Redis connection string
   */
  redisUrl?: string

  /**
   * Name for the main workflow queue that handles retries, step timeouts,
   * and transaction timeouts.
   * @default "medusa-workflows"
   */
  queueName?: string

  /**
   * Name for the job queue that handles scheduled workflow execution.
   * @default "medusa-workflows-jobs"
   */
  jobQueueName?: string

  /**
   * Redis client options
   * @deprecated Use `redisOptions` instead for consistency with other modules
   */
  options?: RedisOptions

  /**
   * Redis client options passed to ioredis
   * @see https://github.com/redis/ioredis#connect-to-redis
   */
  redisOptions?: RedisOptions

  /*
   * =========================================================================
   * Shared Queue/Worker Options
   * =========================================================================
   * These options apply to all queues and workers unless overridden by
   * per-queue specific options below.
   */

  /**
   * Default options for all BullMQ Queue instances.
   * Can be overridden per-queue using `mainQueueOptions`, `jobQueueOptions`,
   * or `cleanerQueueOptions`.
   * @see https://api.docs.bullmq.io/interfaces/v5.QueueOptions.html
   */
  queueOptions?: Omit<QueueOptions, "connection">

  /**
   * Default options for all BullMQ Worker instances.
   * Can be overridden per-worker using `mainWorkerOptions`, `jobWorkerOptions`,
   * or `cleanerWorkerOptions`.
   * @see https://api.docs.bullmq.io/interfaces/v5.WorkerOptions.html
   */
  workerOptions?: Omit<WorkerOptions, "connection">

  /*
   * =========================================================================
   * Per-Queue Options (Main Queue)
   * =========================================================================
   * The main queue handles workflow retries, step timeouts, and transaction
   * timeouts. These are critical real-time operations.
   */

  /**
   * Options specific to the main workflow queue.
   * Overrides `queueOptions` for this queue only.
   * @see https://api.docs.bullmq.io/interfaces/v5.QueueOptions.html
   */
  mainQueueOptions?: Omit<QueueOptions, "connection">

  /**
   * Options specific to the main workflow worker.
   * Overrides `workerOptions` for this worker only.
   * @see https://api.docs.bullmq.io/interfaces/v5.WorkerOptions.html
   */
  mainWorkerOptions?: Omit<WorkerOptions, "connection">

  /*
   * =========================================================================
   * Per-Queue Options (Job Queue)
   * =========================================================================
   * The job queue handles scheduled workflow execution. You may want different
   * concurrency settings for scheduled vs real-time workflows.
   */

  /**
   * Options specific to the job queue (scheduled workflows).
   * Overrides `queueOptions` for this queue only.
   * @see https://api.docs.bullmq.io/interfaces/v5.QueueOptions.html
   */
  jobQueueOptions?: Omit<QueueOptions, "connection">

  /**
   * Options specific to the job worker (scheduled workflows).
   * Overrides `workerOptions` for this worker only.
   * @see https://api.docs.bullmq.io/interfaces/v5.WorkerOptions.html
   */
  jobWorkerOptions?: Omit<WorkerOptions, "connection">

  /*
   * =========================================================================
   * Per-Queue Options (Cleaner Queue)
   * =========================================================================
   * The cleaner queue runs periodically (every 30 minutes) to remove expired
   * workflow executions. This is a low-priority background task.
   */

  /**
   * Options specific to the cleaner queue.
   * Overrides `queueOptions` for this queue only.
   * @see https://api.docs.bullmq.io/interfaces/v5.QueueOptions.html
   */
  cleanerQueueOptions?: Omit<QueueOptions, "connection">

  /**
   * Options specific to the cleaner worker.
   * Overrides `workerOptions` for this worker only.
   * @see https://api.docs.bullmq.io/interfaces/v5.WorkerOptions.html
   */
  cleanerWorkerOptions?: Omit<WorkerOptions, "connection">

  /**
   * Optional separate connection string and options for pub/sub.
   * If not provided, uses the main Redis connection.
   */
  pubsub?: {
    url: string
    options?: RedisOptions
  }
}

declare module "@medusajs/types" {
  interface ModuleOptions {
    "@medusajs/workflow-engine-redis": RedisWorkflowsOptions
    "@medusajs/medusa/workflow-engine-redis": RedisWorkflowsOptions
  }
}

import {
  InternalModuleDeclaration,
  LoaderOptions,
} from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import { asValue } from "@medusajs/framework/awilix"
import Redis from "ioredis"
import { RedisWorkflowsOptions } from "../types"

export default async (
  { container, logger, options, dataLoaderOnly }: LoaderOptions,
  moduleDeclaration: InternalModuleDeclaration
): Promise<void> => {
  const {
    url,
    redisUrl,
    options: deprecatedRedisOptions,
    redisOptions: newRedisOptions,
    jobQueueName,
    queueName,
    // Shared options
    queueOptions,
    workerOptions,
    // Per-queue options
    mainQueueOptions,
    mainWorkerOptions,
    jobQueueOptions,
    jobWorkerOptions,
    cleanerQueueOptions,
    cleanerWorkerOptions,
    pubsub,
  } = options?.redis as RedisWorkflowsOptions

  // Handle backward compatibility for deprecated options
  const resolvedUrl = redisUrl ?? url
  const redisOptions = newRedisOptions ?? deprecatedRedisOptions

  // Log deprecation warnings
  if (url && !redisUrl) {
    logger?.warn(
      "[Workflow-engine-redis] The `url` option is deprecated. Please use `redisUrl` instead for consistency with other modules."
    )
  }
  if (deprecatedRedisOptions && !newRedisOptions) {
    logger?.warn(
      "[Workflow-engine-redis] The `options` option is deprecated. Please use `redisOptions` instead for consistency with other modules."
    )
  }

  // TODO: get default from ENV VAR
  if (!resolvedUrl) {
    throw Error(
      "No `redis.redisUrl` (or deprecated `redis.url`) provided in `workflowOrchestrator` module options. It is required for the Workflow Orchestrator Redis."
    )
  }

  const cnnPubSub = pubsub ?? { url: resolvedUrl, options: redisOptions }

  const queueName_ = queueName ?? "medusa-workflows"
  const jobQueueName_ = jobQueueName ?? "medusa-workflows-jobs"

  // Resolve per-queue options by merging shared defaults with per-queue overrides
  const resolvedMainQueueOptions = {
    ...(queueOptions ?? {}),
    ...(mainQueueOptions ?? {}),
  }
  const resolvedMainWorkerOptions = {
    ...(workerOptions ?? {}),
    ...(mainWorkerOptions ?? {}),
  }
  const resolvedJobQueueOptions = {
    ...(queueOptions ?? {}),
    ...(jobQueueOptions ?? {}),
  }
  const resolvedJobWorkerOptions = {
    ...(workerOptions ?? {}),
    ...(jobWorkerOptions ?? {}),
  }
  const resolvedCleanerQueueOptions = {
    ...(queueOptions ?? {}),
    ...(cleanerQueueOptions ?? {}),
  }
  const resolvedCleanerWorkerOptions = {
    ...(workerOptions ?? {}),
    ...(cleanerWorkerOptions ?? {}),
  }

  let connection
  let redisPublisher
  let redisSubscriber
  let workerConnection

  try {
    connection = await getConnection(resolvedUrl, redisOptions)
    workerConnection = await getConnection(resolvedUrl, {
      ...(redisOptions ?? {}),
      maxRetriesPerRequest: null,
    })
    logger?.info(
      `[Workflow-engine-redis] Connection to Redis in module 'workflow-engine-redis' established`
    )
  } catch (err) {
    logger?.error(
      `[Workflow-engine-redis] An error occurred while connecting to Redis in module 'workflow-engine-redis': ${err}`
    )
  }

  try {
    redisPublisher = await getConnection(cnnPubSub.url, cnnPubSub.options)
    redisSubscriber = await getConnection(cnnPubSub.url, cnnPubSub.options)
    logger?.info(
      `[Workflow-engine-redis] Connection to Redis PubSub in module 'workflow-engine-redis' established`
    )
  } catch (err) {
    logger?.error(
      `[Workflow-engine-redis] An error occurred while connecting to Redis PubSub in module 'workflow-engine-redis': ${err}`
    )
  }

  container.register({
    isWorkerMode: asValue(moduleDeclaration.worker_mode !== "server"),
    partialLoading: asValue(true),
    redisConnection: asValue(connection),
    redisWorkerConnection: asValue(workerConnection),
    redisPublisher: asValue(redisPublisher),
    redisSubscriber: asValue(redisSubscriber),
    redisQueueName: asValue(queueName_),
    redisJobQueueName: asValue(jobQueueName_),
    // Per-queue resolved options
    redisMainQueueOptions: asValue(resolvedMainQueueOptions),
    redisMainWorkerOptions: asValue(resolvedMainWorkerOptions),
    redisJobQueueOptions: asValue(resolvedJobQueueOptions),
    redisJobWorkerOptions: asValue(resolvedJobWorkerOptions),
    redisCleanerQueueOptions: asValue(resolvedCleanerQueueOptions),
    redisCleanerWorkerOptions: asValue(resolvedCleanerWorkerOptions),
    redisDisconnectHandler: asValue(async () => {
      connection.disconnect()
      workerConnection.disconnect()
      redisPublisher.disconnect()
      redisSubscriber.disconnect()
    }),
  })
}

async function getConnection(url, redisOptions) {
  const connection = new Redis(url, {
    lazyConnect: true,
    ...(redisOptions ?? {}),
  })

  await new Promise(async (resolve) => {
    await connection.connect(resolve)
  })

  return connection
}

  private parseFlowOptions() {
    const [steps, features] = TransactionOrchestrator.buildSteps(
      this.definition
    )

    this.options ??= {}

    const hasAsyncSteps = features.hasAsyncSteps
    const hasStepTimeouts = features.hasStepTimeouts
    const hasRetriesTimeout = features.hasRetriesTimeout
    const hasTransactionTimeout = !!this.options.timeout
    const isIdempotent = !!this.options.idempotent

    if (
      hasStepTimeouts ||
      hasRetriesTimeout ||
      hasTransactionTimeout ||
      isIdempotent ||
      this.options.retentionTime ||
      hasAsyncSteps
    ) {
      this.options.store = true
    }

    const parsedOptions = {
      ...this.options,
      hasAsyncSteps,
      hasStepTimeouts,
      hasRetriesTimeout,
    }
    TransactionOrchestrator.workflowOptions[this.id] = parsedOptions

    return [steps, features]

The spec is clear and the right size. Most of it maps onto one place in the code: the `save()` method in each engine's storage class. Before you start, I'd fix two gaps: where the option lives in medusa-config, and what the setting covers. I'd also answer the two open questions.

## How it fits the code

- **Where the change goes.** The logic sits in `save()` in [workflow-engine-inmemory/src/utils/workflow-orchestrator-storage.ts:367-428](packages/modules/workflow-engine-inmemory/src/utils/workflow-orchestrator-storage.ts#L367-L428) and [workflow-engine-redis/src/utils/workflow-orchestrator-storage.ts:545-638](packages/modules/workflow-engine-redis/src/utils/workflow-orchestrator-storage.ts#L545-L638). Today, a finished execution with no `retentionTime` gets deleted. #66 adds a branch for FAILED/REVERTED, and #67 replaces #66's fixed 7 days with the configured value.
- **Seconds is the right unit.** The cleanup query uses `INTERVAL '1 second' * "retention_time"` ([line 764](packages/modules/workflow-engine-inmemory/src/utils/workflow-orchestrator-storage.ts#L764)), the same unit as `retentionTime`.
- **No changes needed to cleanup or the schema.** `clearExpiredExecutions` already covers FAILED and REVERTED, and the `retention_time` column exists in both engines.

## Gaps to fix in the spec

1. **Where the option goes in medusa-config.** The engines don't read options the same way:
   - The Redis engine reads everything from `options.redis` ([loaders/redis.ts:29](packages/modules/workflow-engine-redis/src/loaders/redis.ts#L29)), and the options type `RedisWorkflowsOptions` describes that `redis` block.
   - The in-memory engine has no options type and no loader that reads options.

   Since the setting isn't about Redis, I'd say in the spec that it goes at the top level of `options`, next to `redis`, and that it's the same in both engines. Otherwise the two engines could end up reading it from different places.

2. **The setting only covers stored workflows.** `saveCheckpoint` returns right away if `store` is false ([distributed-transaction.ts:514](packages/core/orchestration/src/transaction/distributed-transaction.ts#L514)). `store` is only turned on for workflows that are idempotent, have async steps, have timeouts or retry intervals, or set `retentionTime` ([transaction-orchestrator.ts:1513-1522](packages/core/orchestration/src/transaction/transaction-orchestrator.ts#L1513-L1522)). A fully synchronous workflow never reaches the storage class, so it is never saved, whatever the option says.
   - This mostly affects #66: its "checkout failed" scenario only works if that workflow is a stored one.
   - It's worth one line in #67 too, so nobody expects every failure to show up: "applies to workflow executions the engine stores".

3. **What "deleted, same as before" means with 0.** Today, child workflows (those with `parentStepIdempotencyKey`) are saved when they finish, with `retention_time` set to null. Nothing ever cleans those rows up. #66 leaves this as an open question. Whatever #66 decides, #67 should say what happens to child runs when the option is 0. My suggestion is "same as today", which means they're still saved.

4. **A workflow that sets `retentionTime: 0`.** The code checks `if (retentionTime)`, so a workflow-level 0 is treated the same as not set. That workflow would get the module's window, even though criterion 5 says the workflow's own value wins. Either the spec says this case counts as "not set", or the check changes to `isDefined`. Changing the check also changes how DONE runs behave, so I'd keep the current behavior and write it down.

5. **Small fixes:**
   - The 0 criterion links "before #16". It should probably point to #66, or say "before #66".
   - "Restart" in the scenario is fine, because options are read once at startup.

## Answers to the open questions

- **Name:** `failedExecutionRetention` is fine. Its docs should say it covers both FAILED and REVERTED. If you'd rather the name say that too, `failedRetentionTime` sits more clearly next to `retentionTime`.
- **Invalid values:** I'd throw a `MedusaError` with `INVALID_DATA` at startup. The fallback option is bad here: a typo would silently keep the 7-day default, which is the opposite of what someone trying to shrink the table wants. The Redis loader already throws at startup when a required option is missing ([loaders/redis.ts:51](packages/modules/workflow-engine-redis/src/loaders/redis.ts#L51)). A non-integer should probably also be rejected, since the column is an `integer`.

## Implementation notes (not needed in the spec)

- **Getting the value into the storage classes.** Both storage classes are registered with `asClass(...).singleton()` and take their dependencies from the container. The simplest route is to register the resolved value with `asValue` in each engine's loader, validating it there, and inject it through the constructor. The in-memory engine's loader ([loaders/utils.ts](packages/modules/workflow-engine-inmemory/src/loaders/utils.ts)) will need to read `options` for this. You'll also need to add a `ModuleOptions` declaration for the in-memory engine, like the Redis one has.
- **When to apply the window.** Only apply the effective window when the state is FAILED or REVERTED. `saveToDb` is also called for in-progress saves, and those should keep `retention_time` null.
- **Tests.** Both engines' integration tests set options through `moduleOptions` in `moduleIntegrationTestRunner`. Testing a custom window, 0 and the default means three runner blocks per engine, or one spec file per case.
- **Order.** #66 has to land first: the 7-day default and the new FAILED/REVERTED branch don't exist yet.

Summary
What

Both workflow engines now keep failed and reverted workflow executions for 7 days by default, instead of deleting them as soon as they finish. Store managers can open them in Settings > Workflows and see which step failed and what was rolled back.

If a stored workflow without its own retentionTime ends as FAILED or REVERTED, its execution is saved with retention_time = 604800 (7 days). The existing clearExpiredExecutions job deletes it after that.
Executions that end as DONE are still deleted when they finish.
A workflow's own retentionTime still applies to every end state.
The change is identical in workflow-engine-inmemory and workflow-engine-redis.
Why

Closes #66

Today a failed run disappears when it finishes, so the only way to debug it is the server logs. The admin list and timeline already exist; they just had nothing to show.

How

In each engine's workflow-orchestrator-storage.ts, a new #getRetentionTime(flow, options) decides the retention value for save():
the workflow's own retentionTime if set,
otherwise the 7-day default for a FAILED or REVERTED run of a non-idempotent workflow,
otherwise nothing.
save()'s existing finish logic is unchanged. A run that gets a retention value is saved instead of deleted.
The default is held in a failedExecutionRetentionTime_ field on the storage class, so Let stores configure how long failed workflow executions are kept #67 can set it from module options.
No changes to orchestration, the API, or the dashboard.
A changeset is included (patch).
Testing

Each engine's integration-tests/__tests__/index.spec.ts has a new block, "Failed and reverted executions retention", with 7 tests. They use store: true workflows:

REVERTED run is kept with 604800
FAILED run (compensation throws) is kept with 604800
DONE run is still deleted
the workflow's own retentionTime: 60 wins on failure
a failed child workflow is kept with the default, and so is its parent, which ends FAILED
an idempotent workflow's failed run is deleted, and retrying with the same transaction ID runs it again
the cleanup job removes a kept run only after its window passes
The HTTP test in integration-tests/http/__tests__/workflow-engine/admin/index.spec.ts checks that GET /admin/workflows-executions lists a reverted run. It also checks that the detail endpoint returns the failed step and the compensated step, which is the data the timeline draws.

Strategy: the "kept" tests fail on develop, and I confirmed that. The DONE, own-retention and idempotent tests pass on both and guard against regressions. Deleting the idempotent check makes the idempotent test fail.

Results from a local run:

In-memory integration: 44 passed (37 before)
Redis integration: 40 passed, 4 skipped (33 passed before; the 4 skips already existed)
Redis unit: 20 passed
HTTP workflow-engine: 5 passed
Modules workflow-engine: 6 passed
Manual: in a local store, a stored workflow whose last step fails shows up in Settings > Workflows as REVERTED.
# module tests load dist, so build first
yarn workspace @medusajs/workflow-engine-inmemory build
yarn workspace @medusajs/workflow-engine-redis build
cd packages/modules/workflow-engine-inmemory && yarn test:integration
cd ../workflow-engine-redis && yarn test:integration
cd ../../../integration-tests/http && npx jest __tests__/workflow-engine
Examples
// Stored, no retentionTime: a failed or reverted run is now kept for 7 days
export const syncOrderWorkflow = createWorkflow(
  { name: "sync-order", store: true },
  () => {
    reserveInventoryStep() // compensated
    notifyWarehouseStep() // throws -> run ends "reverted", visible in the admin
  }
)

// Own retentionTime: unchanged, 60 seconds for every end state
createWorkflow({ name: "other", store: true, retentionTime: 60 }, () => { /* ... */ })
Design
Decision: Apply the default only to workflows that already store checkpoints. That's store: true, or any workflow where store is turned on automatically: async steps, timeouts, retry intervals, or idempotent.

Alternatives considered:

Also persist failed runs of non-stored workflows. That needs changes in core/orchestration and adds DB writes to every workflow.
Apply the default inside the orchestrator instead of the engines.
Rationale: Non-stored workflows return from saveCheckpoint() early and never reach the engines, so keeping them is a much larger change. Option A was agreed with the issue author.

Consequences: Plain synchronous workflows still leave no record. completeCartWorkflow already sets its own 3-day retentionTime, so it isn't affected.

Other decisions:

Idempotent workflows excluded: their stored rows are returned on retry, so keeping a failure would turn retries into replays of the old failure for 7 days.
Child workflows included: failed or reverted children were saved with a null retention_time, so the cleanup job never deleted them. They now get the 7-day window.
DONE with hasFailedSteps out of scope: runs that used continueOnPermanentFailure or skipOnPermanentFailure end as DONE and are still deleted. This is a follow-up.
retentionTime: 0 is treated as not set, as it was before, so a failed run gets the default.
The default stays in each engine: Let stores configure how long failed workflow executions are kept #67 makes it a module option per engine, so a shared constant wasn't needed.
Tech Debt
Introduced:

The same helper is duplicated in both engines. That matches how the two storage classes are already duplicated.
Tests set the private failedExecutionRetentionTime_ field to exercise cleanup. The existing cleaner test already reaches into private storage the same way.
Encountered:

The in-memory engine decides whether a run has finished before merging parallel checkpoints, so a merge can move the state forward after that check. I left this as is, but compute retention after the merge so that runs whose merged state is REVERTED still get the window.
Finished DONE child executions are saved with a null retention_time and never cleaned up. Left as a follow-up.
Module integration tests run against dist, so they need a build after source changes.
Checklist
 I have added a changeset for this PR
 The changes are covered by relevant tests
 I have verified the code works as intended locally
 I have linked the related issue(s) if applicable
Additional Context
CI: CI is configured through workflows inherited from upstream Medusa, but GitHub Actions doesn't currently run them in this repository. No new dependencies or config. The Redis tests need Redis, the same as the existing suite.

Limitations:

A stored scheduled workflow that fails every run adds a row per run for 7 days. A job that runs every minute adds about 10,000 rows a week. Let stores configure how long failed workflow executions are kept #67 adds the setting to shorten or turn off the window.
The docs (store-executions, debug-workflows) don't mention the new default yet. That's a docs follow-up.
Follow-ups: keep DONE runs that have hasFailedSteps, and clean up DONE child executions.

Decided with the teammate who wrote the spec (2026-10-26): **Option A**.

**Why:** Agreed before implementation; list in the PR description per [[pr-description-format]].
**How to apply:** Implement only in the two engines' storage `save()`.

Yes. With #66 merged, two of #67's open questions are still unanswered, and #66's decisions raise two more. I'd send the issue creator these four.

## Questions for the issue creator

1. **What should the option be called?** This is still open in the issue. The merged code calls the internal field `failedExecutionRetentionTime_` ([workflow-orchestrator-storage.ts:123](packages/modules/workflow-engine-inmemory/src/utils/workflow-orchestrator-storage.ts#L123)). So `failedExecutionRetentionTime` is the obvious candidate: it matches the field and reads well next to `retentionTime`. The issue suggests `failedExecutionRetention`. Either works; they just need to pick one.

2. **Should a bad value fail at startup or fall back to the default?** Also still open in the issue. I'd recommend failing at startup with a `MedusaError` (`INVALID_DATA`) for negative, non-number or non-integer values. A silent fallback would keep 7 days when someone is trying to shrink the table, and the `retention_time` column is an integer.

3. **What happens to failed child workflows when the option is 0?** The 0 criterion says "deleted when they finish, the same as before #66." But before #66, failed child runs were not deleted. They were saved with a null `retention_time`, and cleanup never removed them. #66 fixed that by giving them the window, so 0 now has three possible meanings for children:
   - Keep them with a null retention, as before #66. This brings the leak back.
   - Delete them like top-level runs. This is new behavior for children, and could affect how parent workflows find their child runs.
   - Treat 0 as "off" for top-level runs only. Children keep a short window or the default.

   This is the one that most needs their answer, because the criterion as written describes behavior that no longer matches the code.

4. **Should changing the option affect runs that are already kept?** Each row's `retention_time` is fixed when the run finishes. If someone lowers the option from 7 days to 1, runs kept before the restart still last 7 days, and only new failures get 1 day. The scenario says "failed executions now disappear after a day," which suggests existing rows change too. Making them change would mean changing the cleanup, and the issue lists "changing how the cleanup runs" as out of scope. I'd suggest they accept "applies to new failures only" and reword the scenario.

## Where the option goes

There's also a decision that you could make yourselves or confirm with them: where the option lives in medusa-config. The Redis engine reads its settings from `options.redis`, and the in-memory engine reads no options at all yet. I'd put the new option at the top level of `options` in both engines, next to `redis` rather than inside it, and note that in the PR. Ask if you'd rather not decide it yourselves.

## Already settled by #66

These don't need questions, but they belong in the #67 PR's design section:
- The option only affects stored workflows (option A).
- Idempotent workflows are still deleted when they finish, whatever the option says.
- A workflow-level `retentionTime: 0` counts as not set, so it gets the module option.
- DONE runs, including ones with `hasFailedSteps`, are unaffected.

The issue text should also say "stored workflow executions" rather than all failures, and its link to "#16" should point to #66.

Once they answer, I can save the answers to memory as #67 design decisions, the way the #66 ones were saved.

I saved both answers to memory as #67 design decisions, so they'll go in the PR's design section.

**Answer 1 means more than setting the value to 0.** When a run has no retention value, `save()` deletes top-level runs but saves child runs with a null retention, the pre-#66 behavior. So with the option at 0, `#getRetentionTime()` returns nothing for a failed child and the child takes the "save with null" path, not the delete. You'll need to change the child branch of `save()` in both engines: when the option is 0 and the run ended FAILED or REVERTED, delete it whether or not it's a child.

**Possible risk.** I searched for code that reads a finished child's row after it ends and found none. The parent only passes `parentStepIdempotencyKey` along in the run context. Still, add a test where the option is 0, a child fails and the parent fails after it. It should check that the parent finishes as FAILED or REVERTED and the child's row is gone.

**Answer 2 needs no code change.** Kept rows already expire on the retention saved with them. The issue's scenario should say the new window applies to failures after the restart.

You still need to decide the option name, how bad values are handled, and where the option sits in medusa-config. Tell me what you pick and I'll add it to the same memory file.

function calculateDelayFromExpression(expression: CronExpression): number {
  const nextTime = expression.next().getTime()
  const now = Date.now()
  const delay = nextTime - now

  // If the calculated delay is negative or zero, get the next occurrence
  if (delay <= 0) {
    const nextNextTime = expression.next().getTime()
    return Math.max(1, nextNextTime - now)
  }

  return delay
}

function parseNextExecution(
  optionsOrExpression: SchedulerOptions | CronExpression | string | number
) {
  if (typeof optionsOrExpression === "object") {
    if ("cron" in optionsOrExpression) {
      const expression = parseExpression(optionsOrExpression.cron)
      return calculateDelayFromExpression(expression)
    }

    if ("interval" in optionsOrExpression) {
      return optionsOrExpression.interval
    }

    return calculateDelayFromExpression(optionsOrExpression)
  }

  const result = parseInt(`${optionsOrExpression}`)

  if (isNaN(result)) {
    const expression = parseExpression(`${optionsOrExpression}`)
    return calculateDelayFromExpression(expression)
  }

  return result
}

import { asClass, asValue } from "@medusajs/framework/awilix"
import { isDefined, MedusaError } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import { InMemoryDistributedTransactionStorage } from "../utils"

export default async ({ container, options }): Promise<void> => {
  const failedExecutionRetentionTime = options?.failedExecutionRetentionTime

  if (
    isDefined(failedExecutionRetentionTime) &&
    (!Number.isInteger(failedExecutionRetentionTime) ||
      failedExecutionRetentionTime < 0)
  ) {
    throw new MedusaError(
      MedusaError.Types.INVALID_ARGUMENT,
      `The workflow engine module option "failedExecutionRetentionTime" must be a non-negative integer number of seconds. Received: ${failedExecutionRetentionTime}`
    )
  }

  container.register({
    failedExecutionRetentionTime: asValue(failedExecutionRetentionTime),
    inMemoryDistributedTransactionStorage: asClass(
      InMemoryDistributedTransactionStorage
    ).singleton(),
  })
}

export default async ({
  container,
  options,
  dataLoaderOnly,

  const failedExecutionRetentionTime = options?.failedExecutionRetentionTime

  if (

      failedExecutionRetentionTime < 0)
  ) {

      MedusaError.Types.INVALID_ARGUMENT,
      `The workflow engine module option "failedExecutionRetentionTime" must be a non-negative integer number of seconds. Received: ${failedExecutionRetentionTime}`

  })
}

import { TransactionState } from "@medusajs/framework/orchestration"
import { IWorkflowEngineService } from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import { Modules } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import {
  createStep,
  createWorkflow,
  StepResponse,
  WorkflowResponse,
} from "@medusajs/framework/workflows-sdk"
import { moduleIntegrationTestRunner } from "@medusajs/test-utils"
import { ulid } from "ulid"

jest.setTimeout(60000)

const SEVEN_DAYS_IN_SECONDS = 60 * 60 * 24 * 7
const ONE_DAY_IN_SECONDS = 60 * 60 * 24

const createRevertingWorkflow = (config: { retentionTime?: number } = {}) => {
  const workflowId = "reverting-workflow-" + ulid()
  const revertingStep = createStep(
    "reverting-step-" + ulid(),
    () => {
      throw new Error("I am reverting")
    },
    () => {
      return new StepResponse("reverted")
    }
  )

  createWorkflow({ name: workflowId, store: true, ...config }, () => {
    revertingStep()
    return new WorkflowResponse("reverted")
  })

  return workflowId
}

const createFailingWorkflow = () => {
  const workflowId = "failed-workflow-" + ulid()
  const step1 = createStep(
    "step-1-" + ulid(),
    () => {
      return new StepResponse("step 1 done")
    },
    () => {
      throw new Error("I can't compensate")
    }
  )
  const failingStep = createStep("failing-step-" + ulid(), () => {
    throw new Error("I am failing")
  })

  createWorkflow({ name: workflowId, store: true }, () => {
    step1()
    failingStep()
    return new WorkflowResponse("failed")
  })

  return workflowId
}

const createParentAndChildWorkflows = () => {
  const childWorkflowId = "child-workflow-" + ulid()
  const parentWorkflowId = "parent-workflow-" + ulid()
  const failingStep = createStep("child-failing-step-" + ulid(), () => {
    throw new Error("I am failing")
  })

  const childWorkflow = createWorkflow(
    { name: childWorkflowId, store: true },
    () => {
      failingStep()
      return new WorkflowResponse("child")
    }
  )

  createWorkflow({ name: parentWorkflowId, store: true }, () => {
    childWorkflow.runAsStep({ input: {} })
    return new WorkflowResponse("parent")
  })

  return { childWorkflowId, parentWorkflowId }
}

      }

      },
      async (transaction, stepContext) => {
        // The step itself has failed, there is nothing to revert

        const { container, ...sharedContext } = stepContext
        const isAsync = stepContext[" stepDefinition"]?.async

        const workflowEngine = container.resolve(Modules.WORKFLOW_ENGINE, {
          allowUnregistered: true,
        }) as IWorkflowEngineService

        const executionContext = {
          ...(sharedContext?.context ?? {}),
          transactionId: buildTransactionId(step, stepContext),
          parentStepIdempotencyKey: stepContext.idempotencyKey,
          preventReleaseEvents: true,
          cancelingFromParentStep: true,
        }

        if (workflowEngine && isAsync) {
          await workflowEngine.cancel(name, {
            transactionId: executionContext.transactionId,
            context: executionContext,
          })
        } else {
          await workflow(container).cancel({
            transaction: ((transaction as WorkflowResult<any>) ?? {})
              ?.transaction,
            transactionId: executionContext.transactionId,
            container,
            context: executionContext,
          })
        }

        return
      }
    )(input) as ReturnType<StepFunction<TData, TResult>>

    return step
  }

  return mainFlow as ReturnWorkflow<TData, TResult, THooks>
}
```
</details></tool-use>

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-28 13:37:18Z)**_

#67 is implemented in both engines with tests for every acceptance criterion. Everything passes; nothing is committed yet.

**What changed (the same in both engines):**
- **Reading the option:** each engine's loader in `src/loaders/utils.ts` reads `failedExecutionRetentionTime` from the top level of the module `options`. A negative, non-integer or non-number value stops startup with a `MedusaError` (`INVALID_ARGUMENT`).
- **Using it:** the storage class takes the value in its constructor and falls back to 7 days when it isn't set.
- **Option at 0:** `save()` in `workflow-orchestrator-storage.ts` now deletes failed or reverted child runs, as the issue creator asked. A new helper, `#usesFailedExecutionRetention()`, is shared with `#getRetentionTime()`.
- **Supporting changes:** the new spec is added to both `test:integration` scripts, and there's a patch changeset in `.changeset/configure-failed-execution-retention.md`.

**Tests, per engine:**
- **Loader unit tests (7):** 0 and positive values are accepted, an unset option stays unset, and -1, 1.5, `"86400"` and `NaN` are rejected.
- **Integration tests (10), in `failed-execution-retention.spec.ts`:**
  - Option set to one day: reverted, failed, and child plus parent runs are kept for one day, and a workflow's own `retentionTime` still wins.
  - Option set to 0: reverted, failed, and child plus parent runs are deleted, a failed child is deleted while its parent is kept by its own `retentionTime`, and the workflow's own value still wins.
  - Option not set: the 7-day default is used.

**Checking that the tests catch the change:** with the source changes removed, 6 of the 10 integration tests fail. The other tests cover behavior that already existed and act as regression guards. With only the child-branch change removed, the parent-kept test fails.

**Full runs:**
- In-memory: 44 integration and 7 unit tests passed.
- Redis: 40 integration tests passed with 4 skipped (the same counts #66 reported, now plus the new file's 10), and 27 unit tests passed.
- HTTP workflow-engine: 5 passed.

**Something I found while testing:** `deleteFromDb` deletes by `run_id`, and child runs share the parent's `runId`. So in the usual case, deleting a parent already deletes its children. The child change only matters when the parent is kept by its own `retentionTime` and the child isn't. That's why the first version of my child test passed even without the change; the parent-kept test replaced it as the real guard. I saved this to memory for the PR's tech-debt section.

**Before you commit:** leave out three files:
- `packages/admin/dashboard/vite.config.mts`, which was already modified before this work.
- The two `.snapshot-medusa-workflows-integration-1.json` files, which the test runs generated.

_**Agent - sidechain (2026-10-28 13:37:34Z)**_

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 10 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most
severe. If nothing survives, return `[]`. Do not call the
ReportFindings tool even if it is available - this review's
output contract is the JSON block above.

import { asClass, asValue } from "@medusajs/framework/awilix"
import { LoaderOptions } from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import { isDefined, MedusaError } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import { RedisDistributedTransactionStorage } from "../utils"

export default async ({
  container,
  options,
  dataLoaderOnly,
}: LoaderOptions<{ failedExecutionRetentionTime?: number }>): Promise<void> => {
  const failedExecutionRetentionTime = options?.failedExecutionRetentionTime

  if (
    isDefined(failedExecutionRetentionTime) &&
    (!Number.isInteger(failedExecutionRetentionTime) ||
      failedExecutionRetentionTime < 0)
  ) {
    throw new MedusaError(
      MedusaError.Types.INVALID_ARGUMENT,
      `The workflow engine module option "failedExecutionRetentionTime" must be a non-negative integer number of seconds. Received: ${failedExecutionRetentionTime}`
    )
  }

  container.register({
    failedExecutionRetentionTime: asValue(failedExecutionRetentionTime),
    redisDistributedTransactionStorage: asClass(
      RedisDistributedTransactionStorage
    ).singleton(),
    dataLoaderOnly: asValue(!!dataLoaderOnly),
  })
}

import { TransactionState } from "@medusajs/framework/orchestration"
import { IWorkflowEngineService } from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import { Modules } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import {
  createStep,
  createWorkflow,
  StepResponse,
  WorkflowResponse,
} from "@medusajs/framework/workflows-sdk"
import { moduleIntegrationTestRunner } from "@medusajs/test-utils"
import { ulid } from "ulid"
import { TestDatabase } from "../utils"

jest.setTimeout(60000)

const testRunId = ulid()

const redisOptions = (suffix: string) => ({
  url: "localhost:6379",
  queueName: `medusa-workflows-${
    process.env.JEST_WORKER_ID ?? "1"
  }-${testRunId}-${suffix}`,
  jobQueueName: `medusa-workflows-jobs-${
    process.env.JEST_WORKER_ID ?? "1"
  }-${testRunId}-${suffix}`,
})

const SEVEN_DAYS_IN_SECONDS = 60 * 60 * 24 * 7
const ONE_DAY_IN_SECONDS = 60 * 60 * 24

const createRevertingWorkflow = (config: { retentionTime?: number } = {}) => {
  const workflowId = "reverting-workflow-" + ulid()
  const revertingStep = createStep(
    "reverting-step-" + ulid(),
    () => {
      throw new Error("I am reverting")
    },
    () => {
      return new StepResponse("reverted")
    }
  )

  createWorkflow({ name: workflowId, store: true, ...config }, () => {
    revertingStep()
    return new WorkflowResponse("reverted")
  })

  return workflowId
}

const createFailingWorkflow = () => {
  const workflowId = "failed-workflow-" + ulid()
  const step1 = createStep(
    "step-1-" + ulid(),
    () => {
      return new StepResponse("step 1 done")
    },
    () => {
      throw new Error("I can't compensate")
    }
  )
  const failingStep = createStep("failing-step-" + ulid(), () => {
    throw new Error("I am failing")
  })

  createWorkflow({ name: workflowId, store: true }, () => {
    step1()
    failingStep()
    return new WorkflowResponse("failed")
  })

  return workflowId
}

const createParentAndChildWorkflows = (
  parentConfig: { retentionTime?: number } = {}
) => {
  const childWorkflowId = "child-workflow-" + ulid()
  const parentWorkflowId = "parent-workflow-" + ulid()
  const failingStep = createStep("child-failing-step-" + ulid(), () => {
    throw new Error("I am failing")
  })

  const childWorkflow = createWorkflow(
    { name: childWorkflowId, store: true },
    () => {
      failingStep()
      return new WorkflowResponse("child")
    }
  )

  createWorkflow(
    { name: parentWorkflowId, store: true, ...parentConfig },
    () => {
      childWorkflow.runAsStep({ input: {} })
      return new WorkflowResponse("parent")
    }
  )

  return { childWorkflowId, parentWorkflowId }
}

moduleIntegrationTestRunner<IWorkflowEngineService>({
  moduleName: Modules.WORKFLOW_ENGINE,
  resolve: __dirname + "/../..",
  moduleOptions: {
    redis: redisOptions("custom"),
    failedExecutionRetentionTime: ONE_DAY_IN_SECONDS,
  },
  testSuite: ({ service: workflowOrcModule }) => {
    describe("Failed execution retention time set to a custom value", function () {
      beforeEach(async () => {
        await TestDatabase.clearTables()
      })

      afterEach(async () => {
        await TestDatabase.clearTables()
      })

      it("should keep a reverted execution with the configured retention time", async () => {
        const workflowId = createRevertingWorkflow()
        const transactionId = "trx-reverted-" + ulid()

        await workflowOrcModule.run(workflowId, {
          transactionId,
          throwOnError: false,
        })

        const executions = await workflowOrcModule.listWorkflowExecutions({
          transaction_id: transactionId,
        })

        expect(executions).toHaveLength(1)
        expect(executions[0]).toEqual(
          expect.objectContaining({
            state: TransactionState.REVERTED,
            retention_time: ONE_DAY_IN_SECONDS,
          })
        )
      })

      it("should keep a failed execution with the configured retention time", async () => {
        const workflowId = createFailingWorkflow()
        const transactionId = "trx-failed-" + ulid()

        await workflowOrcModule.run(workflowId, {
          transactionId,
          throwOnError: false,
        })

        const executions = await workflowOrcModule.listWorkflowExecutions({
          transaction_id: transactionId,
        })

        expect(executions).toHaveLength(1)
        expect(executions[0]).toEqual(
          expect.objectContaining({
            state: TransactionState.FAILED,
            retention_time: ONE_DAY_IN_SECONDS,
          })
        )
      })

      it("should keep a reverted child workflow execution and its failed parent with the configured retention time", async () => {
        const { childWorkflowId, parentWorkflowId } =
          createParentAndChildWorkflows()

        await workflowOrcModule.run(parentWorkflowId, {
          transactionId: "trx-parent-" + ulid(),
          throwOnError: false,
        })

        const [childExecution] = await workflowOrcModule.listWorkflowExecutions(
          { workflow_id: childWorkflowId }
        )

        expect(childExecution).toEqual(
          expect.objectContaining({
            state: TransactionState.REVERTED,
            retention_time: ONE_DAY_IN_SECONDS,
          })
        )

        const [parentExecution] =
          await workflowOrcModule.listWorkflowExecutions({
            workflow_id: parentWorkflowId,
          })

        expect(parentExecution).toEqual(
          expect.objectContaining({
            state: TransactionState.FAILED,
            retention_time: ONE_DAY_IN_SECONDS,
          })
        )
      })

      it("should use the workflow's own retention time for a reverted execution", async () => {
        const workflowId = createRevertingWorkflow({ retentionTime: 60 })
        const transactionId = "trx-own-retention-" + ulid()

        await workflowOrcModule.run(workflowId, {
          transactionId,
          throwOnError: false,
        })

        const executions = await workflowOrcModule.listWorkflowExecutions({
          transaction_id: transactionId,
        })

        expect(executions).toHaveLength(1)
        expect(executions[0]).toEqual(
          expect.objectContaining({
            state: TransactionState.REVERTED,
            retention_time: 60,
          })
        )
      })
    })
  },
})

        const executions = await workflowOrcModule.listWorkflowExecutions({
          transaction_id: transactionId,
        })

        expect(executions).toHaveLength(0)
      })

      it("should delete a failed execution when it finishes", async () => {
        const workflowId = createFailingWorkflow()
        const transactionId = "trx-failed-" + ulid()

        const { transaction } = await workflowOrcModule.run(workflowId, {
          transactionId,
          throwOnError: false,
        })

        expect(transaction.getFlow().state).toEqual(TransactionState.FAILED)

        const executions = await workflowOrcModule.listWorkflowExecutions({
          transaction_id: transactionId,
        })

        expect(executions).toHaveLength(0)
      })

      it("should delete a reverted child workflow execution and its failed parent when they finish", async () => {
        const { childWorkflowId, parentWorkflowId } =
          createParentAndChildWorkflows()

        const { transaction } = await workflowOrcModule.run(parentWorkflowId, {
          transactionId: "trx-parent-" + ulid(),
          throwOnError: false,
        })

        expect(transaction.getFlow().state).toEqual(TransactionState.FAILED)

        const childExecutions = await workflowOrcModule.listWorkflowExecutions({
          workflow_id: childWorkflowId,
        })
        const parentExecutions = await workflowOrcModule.listWorkflowExecutions(
          {
            workflow_id: parentWorkflowId,
          }
        )

        expect(childExecutions).toHaveLength(0)
        expect(parentExecutions).toHaveLength(0)
      })

      it("should delete a reverted child workflow execution when its parent is kept with its own retention time", async () => {
        const { childWorkflowId, parentWorkflowId } =
          createParentAndChildWorkflows({ retentionTime: 60 })

        await workflowOrcModule.run(parentWorkflowId, {
          transactionId: "trx-parent-" + ulid(),
          throwOnError: false,
        })

        const childExecutions = await workflowOrcModule.listWorkflowExecutions({
          workflow_id: childWorkflowId,
        })
        const parentExecutions = await workflowOrcModule.listWorkflowExecutions(
          {
            workflow_id: parentWorkflowId,
          }
        )

        expect(childExecutions).toHaveLength(0)
        expect(parentExecutions).toHaveLength(1)
        expect(parentExecutions[0]).toEqual(
          expect.objectContaining({
            state: TransactionState.FAILED,
            retention_time: 60,
          })
        )
      })

      it("should use the workflow's own retention time for a reverted execution", async () => {
        const workflowId = createRevertingWorkflow({ retentionTime: 60 })
        const transactionId = "trx-own-retention-" + ulid()

        await workflowOrcModule.run(workflowId, {
          transactionId,
          throwOnError: false,
        })

        const executions = await workflowOrcModule.listWorkflowExecutions({
          transaction_id: transactionId,
        })

        expect(executions).toHaveLength(1)
        expect(executions[0]).toEqual(
          expect.objectContaining({
            state: TransactionState.REVERTED,
            retention_time: 60,
          })
        )
      })
    })
  },
})

import utilsLoader from "../utils"

describe("Utils Loader", () => {
  let containerMock: { register: jest.Mock }

  beforeEach(() => {
    containerMock = {
      register: jest.fn(),
    }
  })

  const getRegisteredRetentionTime = () =>
    containerMock.register.mock.calls[0][0].failedExecutionRetentionTime.resolve()

  describe("failedExecutionRetentionTime option", () => {
    it("should register the option when it is a positive integer", async () => {
      await utilsLoader({
        container: containerMock as any,
        options: { failedExecutionRetentionTime: 86400 },
      })

      expect(getRegisteredRetentionTime()).toEqual(86400)
    })

    it("should register the option when it is 0", async () => {
      await utilsLoader({
        container: containerMock as any,
        options: { failedExecutionRetentionTime: 0 },
      })

      expect(getRegisteredRetentionTime()).toEqual(0)
    })

    it("should register undefined when the option is not set", async () => {
      await utilsLoader({ container: containerMock as any, options: {} })

      expect(getRegisteredRetentionTime()).toBeUndefined()
    })

    it.each([-1, 1.5, "86400", NaN])(
      "should throw when the option is %p",
      async (failedExecutionRetentionTime) => {
        await expect(
          utilsLoader({
            container: containerMock as any,
            options: { failedExecutionRetentionTime } as any,
          })
        ).rejects.toThrow(
          `The workflow engine module option "failedExecutionRetentionTime" must be a non-negative integer number of seconds. Received: ${failedExecutionRetentionTime}`
        )

        expect(containerMock.register).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
      }
    )
  })
})

import { Logger } from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import { QueueOptions, WorkerOptions } from "bullmq"
import { RedisOptions } from "ioredis"

export type InitializeModuleInjectableDependencies = {
  logger?: Logger
}

/**
 * Module config type for the Redis Workflow Engine.
 *
 * The workflow engine uses three queues internally:
 * - **Main queue**: Handles workflow retries, step timeouts, and transaction timeouts
 * - **Job queue**: Handles scheduled workflow job execution
 * - **Cleaner queue**: Handles periodic cleanup of expired workflow executions
 *
 * You can configure shared options that apply to all queues/workers, or provide
 * per-queue overrides for fine-grained control.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // Simple configuration - same options for all queues
 * {
 *   redisUrl: "redis://localhost:6379",
 *   queueOptions: { defaultJobOptions: { removeOnComplete: 1000 } },
 *   workerOptions: { concurrency: 10 }
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // Advanced configuration - per-queue overrides
 * {
 *   redisUrl: "redis://localhost:6379",
 *   // Shared defaults
 *   workerOptions: { concurrency: 10 },
 *   // Override for job queue (scheduled workflows)
 *   jobWorkerOptions: { concurrency: 5 },
 *   // Override for cleaner (low priority)
 *   cleanerWorkerOptions: { concurrency: 1 }
 * }
 * ```
 */
export type RedisWorkflowsOptions = {
  /**
   * Redis connection string
   * @deprecated Use `redisUrl` instead for consistency with other modules
   */
  url?: string

  /**
   * Redis connection string
   */
  redisUrl?: string

  /**
   * Name for the main workflow queue that handles retries, step timeouts,
   * and transaction timeouts.
   * @default "medusa-workflows"
   */

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-28 13:42:13Z)**_

The changes are ready for a PR. The review found nothing that breaks the issue's requirements, and I made the one cleanup worth doing. After rebuilding, all tests still pass: in-memory 44 integration and 7 unit, Redis 40 integration (4 skipped) and 27 unit, including the 10 new tests in each engine.

**The cleanup:** I removed the `#usesFailedExecutionRetention()` helper. In the branch where it was used, only "failed and not idempotent" actually mattered, so that check is now written inline. `#getRetentionTime()` is back to its #66 version, and the storage diff is now about 15 lines per engine. I also reverted a line that Prettier had reformatted outside our change.

**One real edge case, not fixed:** the `retention_time` column is a Postgres `integer`, so it can't hold values above 2,147,483,647 seconds (about 68 years). Startup accepts such a value, and then saving the first failed run errors, so that run's record isn't saved. The fix is one more condition in each loader's check. Nobody is likely to set a value that large, so I left it out to keep the change minimal. Say if you want it.

**Review findings I didn't act on:**
- **A workflow's own `retentionTime: 0` gets the module window:** #66 decided 0 counts as not set, so this is intended.
- **With 0, failed child runs are deleted:** that's the issue creator's answer. I found no code that looks up a finished child's row.
- **The validation is copied in both engines:** the two engines' storage code is already duplicated the same way, and #66 did the same.
- **No public type for the option:** you decided against type changes.
- **A number passed as a string (for example from an env var) fails at startup:** the check is strict on purpose, and the error message says an integer is required, so wrapping it in `Number()` fixes it.

When you commit, leave out `packages/admin/dashboard/vite.config.mts` (it was already modified before this work) and the two `.snapshot-medusa-workflows-integration-1.json` files the test runs created.

Answered by the issue creator (2026-10-28):
- Option set to 0: failed/reverted child workflow runs (`parentStepIdempotencyKey` set) are deleted when they finish, the same as top-level runs. They do NOT go back to the pre-#66 save with null retention.
- Changing the option only affects runs that finish after the restart. Rows already kept expire on the retention_time saved with them; no cleanup changes.

- Top level of module `options` in both engines (sibling of `redis`), like cache-inmemory's top-level `ttl`. Read and validated in each engine's loader, registered with `asValue`, injected into the storage class.
- Invalid value (negative, non-number, non-integer) throws at startup in the loader: `MedusaError` `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, as auth/payment/tax loaders do for bad module options.

Decided by the user (2026-10-28): leave the Redis engine's `ModuleOptions` declaration as is. Later (2026-10-28) the user said to do only what the issue asks, so no new in-memory `ModuleOptions` declaration either; no type changes in #67. List the Redis mismatch under Tech Debt (encountered) in the PR.

Carried over from #66: only stored workflows are affected, idempotent workflows are still deleted on finish, a workflow's own `retentionTime: 0` counts as unset, DONE runs are unaffected.

Found while testing (2026-10-28): `deleteFromDb` deletes by `run_id`, and child runs share the parent's `runId`, so deleting a parent also deletes its children. The child-branch change in save() only shows when the parent is kept by its own `retentionTime` and the child isn't; the test for it uses that setup. Put in the PR under Tech Debt (encountered).

**Why:** Agreed before implementation; list in the PR description per [[pr-description-format]].

```markdown
## Summary

**What** — What changes are introduced in this PR?

Both workflow engines accept a new `failedExecutionRetentionTime` module option, in seconds. It sets how long failed and reverted executions are kept, or turns keeping them off.

- A positive value: kept FAILED and REVERTED executions get that retention window instead of the 7-day default from #66.
- `0`: FAILED and REVERTED executions are deleted when they finish, including child workflow executions.
- Not set: the 7-day default is used.
- A workflow's own `retentionTime` still wins, whatever the option is set to.
- An invalid value (negative, not an integer, a string, or above 2147483647) stops startup with an `INVALID_ARGUMENT` error.

**Why** — Why are these changes relevant or necessary?

Closes #67

#66 keeps failed runs for a fixed 7 days. Busy stores need a shorter window or none at all, for example a scheduled workflow that fails every minute adds about 10,000 rows a week.

**How** — How have these changes been implemented?

- Each engine's `loaders/utils.ts` reads the option from the top level of the module `options` (next to `redis` in the Redis engine), validates it, and registers it in the container.
- Each engine's storage class takes the value in its constructor and stores it in the `failedExecutionRetentionTime_` field added in #66, falling back to 7 days.
- In `save()`, a finished execution with no retention value was deleted, except child executions, which were saved. Failed or reverted children of non-idempotent workflows are now deleted too, which only happens when the option is `0`.
- The new spec is added to both `test:integration` scripts.
- A changeset is included (patch).

**Testing** — How have these changes been tested, or how can the reviewer test the feature?

New in each engine:
- `src/loaders/__tests__/utils.spec.ts` (8 tests): accepts a positive value and `0`, leaves an unset option unset, and rejects `-1`, `1.5`, `2147483648`, `"86400"` and `NaN`.
- `integration-tests/__tests__/failed-execution-retention.spec.ts` (10 tests), with one module runner per option value:
  - one day: reverted, failed, and child plus parent runs are kept for one day, and the workflow's own `retentionTime: 60` wins
  - `0`: reverted, failed, and child plus parent runs are deleted, a failed child is deleted while its parent is kept by its own `retentionTime`, and the workflow's own value wins
  - not set: a reverted run is kept for 7 days

Strategy: without the source changes, 6 of the 10 integration tests fail in each engine. The other 4 cover behavior that already existed and guard against regressions. Without only the child-branch change in `save()`, the "child deleted while its parent is kept" test fails.

Results from a local run:
- In-memory integration: 54 passed (44 before)
- In-memory unit: 8 passed (none before)
- Redis integration: 50 passed, 4 skipped (40 passed before; the 4 skips already existed)
- Redis unit: 28 passed (20 before)
- HTTP workflow-engine: 5 passed

```bash
# module tests load dist, so build first
yarn workspace @medusajs/workflow-engine-inmemory build
yarn workspace @medusajs/workflow-engine-redis build
cd packages/modules/workflow-engine-inmemory && yarn test && yarn test:integration
cd ../workflow-engine-redis && yarn test && yarn test:integration
```

---

## Examples

```ts
// medusa-config.ts
modules: [
  {
    resolve: "@medusajs/medusa/workflow-engine-redis",
    options: {
      redis: { redisUrl: process.env.WE_REDIS_URL },
      // keep failed and reverted executions for 1 day; 0 turns keeping them off
      failedExecutionRetentionTime: 60 * 60 * 24,
    },
  },
]
```

---

## Design

**Decision:** Put the option at the top level of each engine's module `options`, and read and validate it in the engine's loader.

**Alternatives considered:**
- Put it inside the Redis engine's `redis` block. The option isn't about Redis, and the in-memory engine has no such block.
- Fall back to the default on an invalid value. A typo would then quietly keep 7 days.

**Rationale:** Matches existing patterns: cache-inmemory's top-level `ttl` option, and the auth, payment and tax loaders, which throw `INVALID_ARGUMENT` for bad module options.

**Consequences:** A misconfigured value stops startup with a clear error instead of being ignored.

**Other decisions:**
- **Name:** `failedExecutionRetentionTime`, in seconds, matching #66's storage field and the workflow-level `retentionTime`.
- **`0` deletes failed child executions** (agreed with the issue author). They don't go back to the pre-#66 behavior of being saved with a null retention that cleanup never removes.
- **Changing the option only affects new failures** (agreed with the issue author). Executions already kept expire on the window saved with them, so the cleanup job doesn't change.
- **Upper bound of 2147483647:** `retention_time` is a Postgres `integer`, so a larger value would make every save of a failed run error.
- **Carried over from #66:** only stored workflows are affected, idempotent workflows are still deleted when they finish, a workflow's own `retentionTime: 0` counts as not set, and DONE runs are unaffected.

---

## Checklist

- [x] I have added a **changeset** for this PR
- [x] The changes are covered by relevant **tests**
- [x] I have verified the code works as intended locally
- [x] I have linked the related issue(s) if applicable

---

## Additional Context

- **CI:** GitHub Actions doesn't currently run the inherited workflows in this repository. No new dependencies. The Redis tests need Redis, the same as the existing suite.
- **Limitations:** The option has no TypeScript type (see Tech Debt), and the docs don't mention it yet.

---

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:** The validation is duplicated in both engines' loaders, matching how the two storage classes are already duplicated.

**Encountered:**
- The Redis engine's `ModuleOptions` declaration types `options` as the Redis settings themselves, but the code and docs read them from `options.redis`. Left as is to keep this PR to the issue, so the new option has no type in either engine.
- `deleteFromDb` deletes by `run_id`, and child executions share their parent's `runId`, so deleting a parent already deletes its children. The child change in `save()` only matters when the parent is kept by its own `retentionTime`, and the child test uses that setup.
```

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-15 00:11:18Z)**_

**Root cause:** it wasn't a bug in the tooltip change at all — the standalone `yarn workspace @medusajs/dashboard dev` command had a pre-existing config gap. Vite's top-level `define` (used for `__BASE__`, `__BACKEND_URL__`, etc.) only takes effect during production builds or SSR; the plain dev server transforms `.ts`/`.tsx` files through esbuild directly and ignores `define` entirely, so it's had *zero* effect since before I touched anything — I confirmed `__BASE__` (untouched by any of my edits) was equally unresolved. It just happened to surface as a crash the moment `client.ts` tried to read `__AUTH_TYPE__` early in module evaluation.

**Fix, in [vite.config.mts](packages/admin/dashboard/vite.config.mts):**
- Added the same values under `esbuild: { define: {...} }`, which is the option esbuild's dev-mode file transform actually reads.
- Guarded against esbuild rejecting an actual `undefined` value (it requires every define to be a source-code string, unlike Vite's own `define` handling) by falling back to the literal text `"undefined"` instead of `JSON.stringify(undefined)`.

Verified directly against the running server: `client.ts` now evaluates with `backendUrl = "http://localhost:9000"` and `authType = "session"`, `dashboard-app.tsx`'s `basename` resolves to `"/"`, and the server starts and serves `200` with no errors in the log.

Go to `http://localhost:5173/` again — it should load properly now.

import inject from "@medusajs/admin-vite-plugin"
import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react"
import { defineConfig, loadEnv } from "vite"
import inspect from "vite-plugin-inspect"

// https://vitejs.dev/config/
export default defineConfig(({ mode }) => {
  const env = loadEnv(mode, process.cwd())

  const BASE = env.VITE_MEDUSA_BASE || "/"
  const BACKEND_URL = env.VITE_MEDUSA_BACKEND_URL || "http://localhost:9000"
  const STOREFRONT_URL =
    env.VITE_MEDUSA_STOREFRONT_URL || "http://localhost:8000"
  const AUTH_TYPE = env.VITE_MEDUSA_AUTH_TYPE || undefined
  const JWT_TOKEN_STORAGE_KEY =
    env.VITE_MEDUSA_JWT_TOKEN_STORAGE_KEY || undefined
  const MAX_UPLOAD_FILE_SIZE = env.VITE_MEDUSA_MAX_UPLOAD_FILE_SIZE || 1024 * 1024

  /**
   * Add this to your .env file to specify the project to load admin extensions from.
   */
  const MEDUSA_PROJECT = env.VITE_MEDUSA_PROJECT || null
  const sources = MEDUSA_PROJECT ? [MEDUSA_PROJECT] : []

  // esbuild requires every define to be a string of source code, so an unset
  // value is passed as the literal text "undefined" instead of JSON.stringify(undefined)
  const defines = {
    __BASE__: JSON.stringify(BASE),
    __BACKEND_URL__: JSON.stringify(BACKEND_URL),
    __STOREFRONT_URL__: JSON.stringify(STOREFRONT_URL),
    __AUTH_TYPE__: AUTH_TYPE ? JSON.stringify(AUTH_TYPE) : "undefined",
    __JWT_TOKEN_STORAGE_KEY__: JWT_TOKEN_STORAGE_KEY
      ? JSON.stringify(JWT_TOKEN_STORAGE_KEY)
      : "undefined",
    __MAX_UPLOAD_FILE_SIZE__: JSON.stringify(MAX_UPLOAD_FILE_SIZE),
  }

  return {
    plugins: [
      inspect(),
      react(),
      inject({
        sources,
      }),
    ],
    // `define` above only applies to production builds and SSR; the plain
    // dev server transforms first-party .ts/.tsx files through esbuild
    // directly and only reads `esbuild.define`, so it has to be repeated
    // here for these globals to be replaced while running `vite dev`.
    define: defines,
    esbuild: {
      define: defines,
    },
    server: {
      open: true,
    },
  }
})
